synthesis:draft.headline: SA1 forecast review (targets 2026-07-30 11:00 UTC to 2026-07-30 23:00 UTC): MAE 32.88 MW, mean error 4.88 MW, 24 paired half‑hours.
summary: Over the 24 paired half‑hours the forecast POE50 vs actual comparison reported MAE 32.88 MW [ev0653].
The mean error (POE50 − actual) over the 24 half‑hours was +4.88 MW [ev0654].

At the half‑hour ending 2026-07-30T17:00:00Z (2026-07-31 02:30 ACST) POE50 = 1520.0 MW and actual operational demand = 1466.0 MW; the forecast error was +54.0 MW (3.68%) [ev0601, ev0602, ev0603, ev0604].
The largest absolute single half‑hour error in the window was 66.0 MW (4.2%) [ev0591, ev0592].
The compare routine paired 24 forecast/actual intervals for this target window [ev0655].

numeric_claims.text: forecast error = 54.0 MW (POE50 − actual) for half‑hour ending 2026-07-30T17:00:00Z
POE50 = 1636.0 MW for the interval with largest absolute error
actual = 1570.0 MW for the interval with largest absolute error

possible_explanations.statement: Short‑term variability in realised demand or unobserved local demand drivers may have made actual demand differ from the forecast.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare higher‑frequency demand or SCADA traces and local event logs for the intervals with larger errors to see if sudden changes in measured demand coincide with the errors.

possible_explanations.statement: Differences between the forecast model inputs (for example weather or interconnector flows used by the run) and the inputs observed in real time might have produced the errors.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare the forecast run issuance times and the input datasets used by those runs with the observed weather and interconnector flow data for the same intervals.

possible_explanations.statement: Local generation outages or dispatch interventions might have affected net operational demand in the intervals with larger absolute errors.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Check outage and dispatch event logs (AEMO intervention/market event records) for the specific half‑hours that show the largest errors.
